Question B-003-005-006.

Why the correct answer is right: The intermediate frequency (IF) amplifier supplies most of the receiver gain after the signal has been converted and filtered.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Boost the signal as required for the mixer": Mixer drive is provided by the local oscillator. The IF amplifier comes after the mixer rather than boosting a signal for it.
- sourceIndex 2: "Increase the level of the recovered modulation": Recovered modulation is audio, so increasing that level is the audio-frequency (AF) amplifier's job after detection.
- sourceIndex 3: "Provide sufficient gain to activate the limiter circuit": A limiter circuit is a frequency-modulation (FM) block. It is not the purpose of the intermediate-frequency (IF) amplifier used for single-sideband (SSB) and continuous-wave (CW) reception.
